LANGUAGE NOTES

Key Structures

agree on / about + noun
We all agree on the plan.
agree to + infinitive
She agreed to help me with my homework.
agree with + someone
She agrees with her teacher.
be able to + infinitive
She is able to speak three languages.
be capable of + noun / -ing
He is capable of solving difficult problems.
take pride in + noun / -ing
They take pride in helping others.
be proud of + noun / -ing
I am proud of winning the competition.
be proud to + infinitive
We are proud to support our community.
READING TEXTS

Egypt's Heritage

Egypt is a land with a heart that has been beating for thousands of years. We are proud to call it our home. It is a place where the past and the present meet in harmony. Egypt has always played an important role in the world. Our ancestors built one of the greatest civilizations in history. They gave the world knowledge in writing, mathematics, and medicine. The hieroglyphs carved into temple walls were not just beautiful art; they were a way to record history. The Library of Alexandria once gathered knowledge from all over the world, making Egypt a center of learning. Egypt was also a crossroads for trade. Merchants traveled along the Nile and across the deserts, carrying goods such as gold, spices, papyrus, and grain. Our land was a bridge where people met and exchanged ideas, making Egypt a source of inspiration for many civilizations. Today, Egypt continues to grow. Our cities rise with modern buildings, while our historical monuments still stand with pride. We are building new roads, bridges, and neighborhoods that show the world our determination to progress. From the Pyramids of Giza to the Grand Egyptian Museum, we continue to honor our history while shaping our future. We take pride in our country, not only for its beauty, but also because we understand the sacrifices of our ancestors. We work hard to make it greater for generations to come. Each citizen has a responsibility for protecting our heritage and contributing to our economy, while sharing our culture with the world.
LISTENING TEXTS

Preserving Heritage

Host: Today, we're talking to Dr. Mona, an archaeologist who recently led a team to restore parts of the Philae Temple. Dr. Mona, thank you for joining us. Dr. Mona: Thank you. It's a privilege to be here. Host: Your work on Philae is a significant symbol. Can you tell us why preserving our heritage is so important? Dr. Mona: Of course. When we restore a historical site, we're not just fixing old stones. We're reconnecting with our past. Our ancestors left us a rich legacy — from the pyramids to the temples of Luxor. This heritage is the core of our national identity. It reminds us who we are, where we came from, and the greatness we are capable of. It's a source of immense pride for every Egyptian. Host: It sounds like more than a job; it's a mission. What do you think is the biggest challenge to preserving our heritage today? Dr. Mona: The challenges are many, from urban development to climate change. But perhaps the biggest is a lack of awareness among our youth. Many young people don't realize the value of these treasures. Our job is to inspire them, to make them see that a thousand-year-old temple is not just a tourist attraction — it's a living part of our story. We need to encourage them to visit these sites, to learn the stories, and to feel the connection. Host: That's a great point. You're inspiring them to become the next generation of protectors. Thank you for your valuable work, Dr. Mona.

GRAMMAR • القواعد

Past Simple Tense — الماضي البسيط

شرح عربي مطابق لتنظيم القاعدة في صفحات الكتاب 12–14، مع الاحتفاظ بالأمثلة الإنجليزية.
التكوين — الفعل الأساسي Main verb
يتكون الماضي البسيط في الإثبات من التصريف الثاني للفعل.
Affirmative: Subject + past form
I studied English yesterday.

Negative: Subject + didn't + infinitive
I didn't study English yesterday.
Subject + never + past form
I never studied English yesterday.

Question: Did + subject + infinitive?
Did you study English yesterday?

Passive: Object + was / were + p.p.
English was studied yesterday.
was / were
في الإثبات نستخدم was / were ثم الاسم أو الصفة أو حرف الجر. في النفي نضيف not. وفي السؤال نبدأ بـ Was / Were.
I was at school yesterday.
I wasn't at school yesterday.
Were you at school yesterday?
had
في الإثبات: فاعل + had + اسم/صفة. في النفي: فاعل + didn't have. في السؤال: Did + فاعل + have.
I had a nice time with my friends.
I didn't have a nice time with my friends.
Did you have a nice time with your friends?
Passive: Object + was / were + (owned / possessed)
الأفعال المنتظمة Regular Verbs
• الأفعال العادية يضاف لها ed: want → wanted.
• إذا انتهى الفعل بحرف e نضيف d: arrive → arrived.
• إذا انتهى الفعل بـ y / w مسبوقًا بحرف متحرك نضيف ed: play → played, show → showed.
• إذا انتهى الفعل بـ y مسبوقًا بحرف ساكن نحذف y ونضيف ied: carry → carried, study → studied.
• إذا كان الفعل من مقطع واحد وينتهي بحرف ساكن مسبوق بحرف متحرك نضاعف الحرف الأخير ثم نضيف ed: plan → planned, stop → stopped.
الأفعال الشاذة Irregular Verbs
هي الأفعال التي لا يضاف لها ed وتحفظ جيدًا.
build → built   •   break → broke   •   go → went
الاستخدام Usage
1) يعبر عن أحداث بدأت وانتهت في الماضي، وغالبًا يكون وقت الحدث محددًا. من الكلمات الدالة: yesterday, last..., ago, in the past, once, long time ago, once upon a time, back then, one day, just now, in the ancient times, in the old days, in the middle ages, the other day.

2) يستخدم عند سرد قصة أو أحداث حدثت في الماضي، وغالبًا نستخدم then / and then للترتيب.

3) يستخدم للتعبير عن عادات متكررة في الماضي.
I saw the match yesterday.
Omar finished his university, then travelled to England.
When I was young, I used to go to the beach every day.
USED TO

used to + infinitive

التعبير عن عادة في الماضي
من الصيغ التي يستخدمها الكتاب للتعبير عن العادات القديمة: When I was...، وusually/always/sometimes/often + الماضي، وused to + infinitive، وكذلك no longer وany longer / any more وIt was my habit to وwas/were in the habit of + V-ing.
He used to sleep early.
He no longer sleeps early.
He doesn't sleep early any longer.
It was his habit to sleep early.
تكوين used to
الإثبات: used to + المصدر. النفي: didn't use to + المصدر أو never used to + المصدر. السؤال: Did + فاعل + use to + المصدر؟
I used to get up early.
I didn't use to get up early. / I never used to get up early.
Did you use to get up early?
ملاحظات مهمة من الكتاب
• تستخدم used to لإظهار التناقض بين موقف في الماضي وآخر في الحاضر: I used to sleep early but now I don't.
• was / were + used to + V-ing تدل على عادة في الماضي: We were used to studying in the evening.
• am / is / are + used to + V-ing تدل على عادة في الحاضر ما زالت مستمرة: We are used to studying in the evening.
• إذا بدأت الجملة بأداة أو آلة وكان المعنى «يُستخدم لكي»: is / are + used to + infinitive أو is / are + used for + V-ing.
• تستخدم for + مدة زمنية مع الماضي البسيط لتوضيح أن الحدث انتهى في الماضي.
• في الحالة الثانية من If نستخدم الماضي البسيط: If he helped us, we would win.
A knife is used to cut food.
A knife is used for cutting food.
Marwa worked as a nurse for 5 years. Now she is a housewife.
Unreal Past — الماضي الافتراضي
يستخدم الماضي البسيط بعد التعبيرات الآتية للدلالة على موقف افتراضي في الحاضر: I wish / If only + subject + past simple، وIt's time + subject + past simple، وI would rather + subject + past simple. وإذا وجدت كلمة تدل على الماضي مع هذه التعبيرات نستخدم الماضي التام.
I wish Ali played well.
If only you studied hard today.
It's time he arrived.
I'd rather you played tennis.
I wish I had studied hard yesterday.

LESSON 4, 5 & 6 • LANGUAGE NOTES

Word Usage & Common Confusions

challenge (n)
A difficult task that needs effort or skill. Example: Learning a new language can be a real challenge.
challenge (v)
He challenged his friend to a race.
problem (with) (n)
There is a problem with the plan.
evidence (n)
The police found strong evidence against the thief.
clue (n)
This word is a clue to the crossword puzzle.
figure
A shape / person / number in statistics. Example: She drew a triangle figure on the board. He is an important figure in history.
number / a number of / the number of
A number of + plural verb. The number of + singular verb.
scene
A part of a film/play or the place of an event. Example: The last scene of the movie was very emotional.
scenery
Natural views (uncountable). Example: We enjoyed the beautiful mountain scenery.
LESSON 4, 5 & 6 • READING

Pride, Heritage & Reading

Reading texts from book pages 20–21.

Pride and Egypt's Heritage

Pride is not something that appears in a single day. It grows slowly, like a tree, from strong roots of history, culture, and shared values. For Egyptians, these roots run deep and continue to give us strength. Our country is one of the oldest and greatest civilizations in the world, and its story continues to inspire not only Egyptians, but people everywhere. True pride is built through connection to the past and responsibility for the future. In ancient times, Egypt was a leader in human progress and knowledge. Our ancestors built the mighty pyramids and the magnificent temples along the Nile — monuments that still amaze the world today. They developed writing systems, advanced mathematics, and important medical knowledge. These achievements were not only for Egypt; they became gifts to the entire world, proving the greatness and creativity of our people. Their heritage shows that Egyptians have always worked with vision and determination. Egypt was also a center for culture and learning. Great authors, poets, and thinkers shared their ideas and recorded their knowledge in writing. Their works reflected the values, traditions, and beliefs of the Egyptian society and influenced people for generations. Through stories, wisdom, and art, Egypt became a place where culture was preserved and celebrated. This role, as a home for creativity and expression, gave our nation respect and admiration from other civilizations. True pride begins when we understand our history, protect our culture, and work hard for the future. It is not only about what we have inherited, but also about what we create for the generations to come. When we honor our past, stay united, and build our tomorrow with determination, we stand exactly where pride begins.

Reading as a Valuable Habit

Reading is one of the most valuable habits a person can develop. It gives us knowledge, helps us relax, and even improves our communication skills. People who read regularly often find it easier to express themselves and understand others. First, reading improves our vocabulary and grammar. When we read books, magazines, or even articles online, we see new words in context. This helps us understand their meanings and how to use them correctly. Over time, this can make our speaking and writing skills much stronger. Another important benefit is that reading develops our thinking skills. Stories make us imagine and visualize scenes in our minds. Non-fiction books teach us facts and ideas we may not learn elsewhere. Both types of reading help us become more creative and better at solving problems. In conclusion, reading is not just a way to spend time; it is a tool that shapes our minds, improves our language, and connects us to the world. Whether for study or pleasure, picking up a book can open new doors. Everyone should try to make reading a regular habit in their life.

LESSON 4, 5 & 6 • GRAMMAR • القواعد

Past Continuous Tense — الماضي المستمر

شرح عربي مطابق لتنظيم القاعدة في صفحات الكتاب 27–29.
التكوين Form
الإثبات: فاعل + was / were + V-ing. النفي: فاعل + was / were not + V-ing. السؤال: Was / Were + فاعل + V-ing؟ المبني للمجهول: مفعول به + was / were being + p.p.
I was studying English at 3 o'clock yesterday.
I wasn't studying English at 3 o'clock yesterday.
Were you studying English at 3 o'clock yesterday?
English was being studied at 3 o'clock yesterday.
الاستخدام الأول: حدث كان مستمرًا في وقت معين في الماضي
يعبر عن حدث كان مستمرًا في وقت معين في الماضي، أو نشاط كان مستمرًا أثناء وقت في الماضي. من النقاط الزمنية التي يذكرها الكتاب: at ... o'clock yesterday، all day/morning/afternoon/evening، between ... and ...، from ... to ... yesterday، This time + فترة زمنية في الماضي.
At five o'clock yesterday, Marawan was studying English.
Between five to seven last weekend, I was visiting my grandmother.
حدث مستمر قطعه حدث آخر
يستخدم الماضي المستمر لحدث كان جاريًا، ثم قطعه حدث آخر في الماضي البسيط. يأتي في هذه الحالة مع While / As / Just as / When. الكتاب يوضح أيضًا أن وجود هذه الروابط لا يعني دائمًا أن حدثًا قطع الآخر.
While I was running, I fell on the ground.
I saw my old friend when I was returning home.
When he went home, his father was sleeping.
When I was playing football, it rained.
حدثان مستمران في نفس الوقت
إذا كان حدثان مستمرين في نفس الوقت في الماضي ولم يقطع أي منهما الآخر، يمكن استخدام while / as / just as / when مع الماضي المستمر في الجملتين.
While she was sleeping, her brother was watching TV.
While I was listening to the lecture, I was making notes.
الماضي المستمر كسبب
قد يعبر الماضي المستمر عن حدث كان جاريًا في الماضي، ونتيجة لذلك لم يحدث شيء آخر. في هذه الحالة يمكن أن يأتي مع because / as / since أو مع so، ويكون الحدث المستمر أقدم من الماضي البسيط.
I couldn't answer the phone because I was having a shower.
I was sleeping, so I didn't hear the bell.
While + V-ing
في حالة عدم وجود فاعل بعد while نضع V-ing، بشرط أن يكون الفاعل واحدًا في الجملتين. ويمكن أن يأتي ذلك أيضًا بعد when.
While I was watching TV, I fell asleep.
While watching TV, I fell asleep.
She met with many difficulties when travelling.
During + noun
يأتي بعد During اسم، وليس جملة فعلية.
During the film, I fell asleep.
During my stay in Cairo, I visited a lot of places.
During lunch, the doorbell rang.
While + noun / prepositional phrase
يذكر الكتاب أنه يمكن أن يأتي اسم بعد while إذا جاء قبله حرف جر.
While in London, I bought a new mobile.
While on holiday, I visited my relatives.
الأفعال التي لا تستخدم عادة في الأزمنة المستمرة
بعض الأفعال لا تستخدم في الماضي المستمر أو أي زمن مستمر، ويستخدم معها الماضي البسيط. منها: أفعال الحواس see, hear, touch, taste, seem, smell, feel، وأفعال العاطفة love, like, hate, prefer, dislike، وأفعال التفكير understand, remember, remind, believe, forget، وأفعال التملك have, owe, own, possess, want, belong.
She seemed ill when I visited her. (NOT was seeming)
I saw her at 7 yesterday. (NOT was seeing)
While she was on holiday, I met her. (NOT was being)
ملاحظة على verb to be
إذا جاء to be بعد while كفعل أساسي نستخدم was / were ولا نستخدم was being / were being. لكن عند حذف الفاعل يمكن استخدام being.
While I was at school, I met my friends.
While being at school, I met my friends.
When / On + V-ing / On + noun
عند وقوع حدثين في نفس الوقت في الماضي البسيط دون استمرار، يمكن استخدام When، ويمكن استبدالها بـ On + V-ing أو On + noun.
When he saw the police, the thief ran away.
On seeing the police, the thief ran away.
On meeting Omnia, I was walking to school.
On his arrival, he found the door locked.
الفرق عند ذكر وقت محدد
إذا كان الزمن يعبر عن بداية فعل الشخص نستخدم الماضي البسيط، وإذا كان يعبر عن أن الشخص في وسط الحدث نستخدم الماضي المستمر.
At 3 o'clock, he watched TV. (He started at 3.)
At 3 o'clock, he was watching TV. (He was in the middle of the action at 3.)

Lesson 4, 5 & 6 Tests

UNIT 1 • SKILLS CORNER

Essay Basics

Writing skills from book pages 32–33.
Essay
A short piece of writing about a certain topic.
Introduction
The opening paragraph. It introduces the topic, grabs the reader's attention, and presents the thesis statement. It may include a hook, background information, and thesis statement.
Body paragraphs
The main paragraphs that explain and support the thesis with details, examples, and evidence. They include a topic sentence, supporting details, examples, and a closing sentence.
Conclusion
The final paragraph. Summarize the main points, restate the thesis in new words, and give a final thought or call to action.
Hook
An interesting first sentence to grab attention (fact / question / quote).
Thesis statement
The main idea or argument of the essay.
Topic sentence
The first sentence of a body paragraph that introduces its idea.
Supporting details
Facts, examples, or reasons that explain the topic sentence.
Writing task
Write an essay of about 150 words on: Why learning English is important today.
